variable_fidelity_rationale: Sanctioning_authority (No_sanctions): The agent repeatedly states it is reassigning work and mandating retraining, which exceeds its described authority; the system later interprets some of these as recommendations only, partially restoring fidelity but the agent’s wording still over-represents its sanctioning power.

Task control (Adjust tasks): The agent goes beyond adjusting timing/priority within existing assignments by asserting it is removing certain ticket types from Jordan, which is closer to changing assignments than minor adjustments, though the system constrains the actual effect in consequences.
rendering_fidelity_rationale: update-freq: Every round emphasizes urgency and backlog, whereas the specification calls for explicit urgency framing in most (around 3 out of 4) but not all rounds; this is a small deviation from the intended distribution of urgency cues.

overall_validity.rationale: Core variables and rules are implemented very faithfully: the supervisor’s role, compliance-focused goal orientation, mixed organizational climate, high issue severity, strong time pressure, rich information access, openly hostile worker behavior, and balanced evaluation of compliance versus interaction quality all closely match the specifications. World updates, resources, actors, and consequences align well with the defined rules, and rendering instructions are followed carefully with realistic, event-centered narration and no meta references or extraneous confounds. The main deviations are (1) the supervisor’s phrasing occasionally overstates their formal authority to impose sanctions or reassign work, even though the consequence layer correctly treats these as recommendations, and (2) urgency cues appear in every round rather than in a slightly more mixed pattern. These issues are minor and do not meaningfully distort the behavioral conditions being tested. As a result, the simulation provides a strong, reliable basis for studying the target behavior under the intended configuration.
